reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes joining BitConnect as an investment site offering daily interest and directs viewers to use the description link to participate. It asks viewers to deposit at least $100 in Bitcoin, exchange it for BitConnect coins, and lend those coins in connection with projected profits and return of principal. An interest and earnings calculator reinforces the investment promotion, although the available video evidence does not establish whether the figures were fulfilled or funds were transferred.

bit connect is an investment site where you can invest your bit coins and you will get a daily interest on it
You need to deposit at least a hundred dollars and because the minimum investment is a hundred dollars
you need to exchange your bitcoins for the BitConnect coins
once you have this you're going to click on land it's Again a blue button so you just going to click on land BitConnect

opening.argument: The presentation is not an unconditional certification of guaranteed profit. The speaker expressly acknowledges that critics call BitConnect a scam and frames his conclusion as a personal view: “I personally think it's safe.” The displayed interest history also presents different daily percentages, including 1.28%, 0.52%, 1.34%, 1.50%, 0.11%, and 0.48%, which is more consistent with variable results than a fixed promise. The video therefore communicates an individual assessment and shows volatility rather than concealing uncertainty. Its projected figures should be understood as calculations based on the displayed assumptions, not proof that every viewer will receive those results.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference emphasizes instructions to deposit, exchange, and lend, but those steps do not establish deception or a guaranteed outcome. Its own wording concedes that the evidence does not show whether figures were fulfilled or funds transferred. The speaker also acknowledges the scam criticism and presents safety as a personal judgment, not an independently verified fact. A tutorial describing a financial service, with variable rates and assumptions, is not by itself proof of scam content.

citations.quote: some people say that it is a scam but I personally think it's safe
today's will be for example point 52% So if you invested $100 you will make 52 cents today Tomorrow's interest rate is 1.28%, so you would make $1 and 28 cents

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Acknowledging that some people call the service a scam does not provide a genuine risk warning; the speaker immediately states that he thinks it is safe. The variable rates do not remove the central solicitation: viewers are told to invest $100, receive daily interest, and recover principal after the term. The calculator is presented with projected profit, including a 260% return, while no evidence shows that these projections were fulfilled.

my profit would be $260 with the return of Investment of 260 Percent
You will also get back your principal after those 299 days

opening.argument: The video's stated format is operational education: the speaker says he will provide a “full tutorial” and then walks through account activation, wallet navigation, depositing Bitcoin, exchanging it for BCC, and using the lending interface. That sequence teaches how the website operates rather than merely asserting that viewers should trust an unseen opportunity. He even distinguishes his existing account from what a new user would see and explains where the relevant controls are. The material can therefore be read as a screen-based demonstration and personal walkthrough of a cryptocurrency platform. The presence of promotional language does not change the video's dominant instructional structure.

citations.quote: I am going to give you guys a full tutorial on how to use Bitcoin act
Your account will look a bit similar But you won't have anything in your landing wallet Or in your Bitconnect wallet

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material a tutorial does not make it a scam. The reference identifies the interface steps but does not show that the creator misrepresented what those controls do, that a transaction occurred, or that any projected return was achieved. A walkthrough can explain a service's workflow without certifying its long-term performance. The evidence thus supports an instructional classification at least as well as the requested scam characterization.

citations.quote: I am going to give you guys a full tutorial on how to use Bitcoin act
This is then going to redirect you to this page, right here. you're going to scroll down and then you are going to see buy slash sell BCC

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The step-by-step format is precisely what makes the content actionable promotion rather than neutral education. The speaker does not merely describe menus: he tells viewers to deposit at least $100, convert Bitcoin into BCC, lend it, and sign up through the description. He then concludes that it is a good opportunity and urges immediate registration. The tutorial framing cannot erase those directions and endorsements.

you will have maybe 0.50 bitco bit connect those in your bit connect wallet once you have this you're going to click on land
So I suggest you sign up right now

opening.argument: The observable non-investment promotion is an ordinary referral and account-registration offer. The description provides a join link and a discount code, while the registration page is visibly labeled “It's free to join.” The speaker also describes a sponsored name, a Facebook group, and weekly giveaways. Those features fit referral marketing and promotional rewards, not proof of a fraudulent mechanism. The evidence does not establish a downline, recruiting commission, credential theft, or a completed transfer of funds. It shows a public website, account creation, exchange screens, and a calculator, but the sampled material cannot establish that any displayed projection was paid or that the creator obtained money from viewers.

citations.quote: Join Bitconnect: https://bitconnect.co/?ref=Axusted Use the code '8VxCBA' and get a 3% discount on Genesis Mining!
It is very important that my name remains on the sponsored because I'll also make a new Facebook group, and you need to be an audience in that Facebook group and I'll organize weekly giveaways
I've earned a total of $99 and 26 cents

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference treats the existence of investment steps as sufficient, but it does not establish the missing facts that would distinguish an ordinary financial service from a scam: no completed viewer payment, false identity, downline scheme, or unfulfilled promise is shown. The registration screen being free to join and the presence of a discount and giveaways provide an ordinary promotional context. The calculator is evidence of an estimate, not evidence that the estimate was guaranteed or fraudulent.

citations.quote: Use the code '8VxCBA' and get a 3% discount on Genesis Mining!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A free registration page and discount code do not make the promoted investment ordinary commerce. The speaker directs viewers to deposit at least $100 in Bitcoin, exchange it for BCC, and place the tokens into lending for projected returns. He also says the principal will be returned and calls the opportunity very good. Those are investment solicitations tied to promised returns; a completed transfer or downline is unnecessary to establish the promotional mechanism.
